about: A simple language for describing database tables, with tools that convert it to and from SQL.

prs.title: JSON column defaults from Postgres survive the round trip
prs.broken: Reading a Postgres database into DBML lost the quotes and type on JSON column defaults, so turning it back into SQL gave code Postgres refused to run.
prs.changed: JSON defaults are now kept exactly as Postgres reports them, the same way the SQL importer already writes them.
prs.matters: Schemas pulled from a live Postgres database can be turned back into working SQL.

prs.title: Postgres imports keep the double precision type
prs.broken: Importing a Postgres schema with a float column wrote its type as doubleprecision, so the SQL exported from it failed to load in Postgres.
prs.changed: The importer now keeps the space between the two words of the type.
prs.matters: Schemas from pg_dump round-trip back into Postgres.
